notes: Sources read: 2025 Form 740 packet with instructions (40 PDF pages), Schedule M (4 pages), Schedule P (2 pages), and, archived on 2026-11-07, Form 740 (3 pages) and Schedule ITC (8 pages). Page numbers are the PDF's own (pypdf markers), not the printed folios: the differences chart is packet PDF p.9, printed page 7.

Form 740 and Schedule ITC are not inside the packet: packet PDF pp.4, 10, 19, 20, 30 and 34 say 'This page has been intentionally left blank' and PDF p.39 is empty. Both were archived separately on 2026-11-07 (740_2025.pdf and Schedule_ITC_2025.pdf). Form 740 lines cited here were checked against Form 740 PDF pp.1-2: line 17 personal tax credits, line 18 = line 16 less line 17 ('If line 17 is larger than line 16, enter zero'), line 19 the sum of line 18 Columns A and B, line 20 family size, line 21 = line 19 times the Family Size Tax Credit decimal, line 22 = line 19 less line 21.

Flat rate: the booklet prints one rate, 4% (PDF p.3 'For 2025, the tax rate for individual income tax is 4%'; PDF p.13 Line 12 'Multiply line 11 by four percent (.04)'). No separate schedule is printed for any filing status. Kentucky's statuses are Single (including federal head of household and qualifying widow(er)), Married filing separately on a combined return, Married filing joint, and Married filing separate returns (PDF p.13).

Standard deduction 3,270 (PDF p.3, p.13, p.31). Recorded per return because a joint return gets one; on a combined return (Filing Status 2) each spouse enters 3,270, and PDF p.13 says that status is open 'if both you and your spouse had income'. Itemizing on Schedule A is allowed; if one spouse itemizes the other must.

No personal exemption, dependent exemption, age-65 or blindness deduction is printed (not found in the booklet). Chart B (PDF p.11) uses 4,270 and 5,270 for age 65 or over or blind, but those are filing-requirement thresholds, not deductions.

Personal tax credits: Schedule ITC PDF p.2 Section B prints, for the taxpayer (lines 1-3) and for the spouse (lines 5-7, 'Complete only if filing joint or married, filing separately on a combined return'): 'If you were 65 on or before 12/31/2025, enter 40'; 'If you were legally blind on 12/31/2025, enter 40'; 'If you were a member of the Kentucky National Guard on 12/31/2025, enter 20'. Lines 9-12 carry them to Form 740 line 17 (not to exceed 100 a person, 200 joint). Form 740 PDF p.1 line 18 stops them at the tax. who.basis each_person follows the separate taxpayer and spouse lines. Packet PDF p.14 Line 17 and Schedule ITC PDF p.7 say only who completes Section B.

Family Size Tax Credit: the table is Schedule ITC PDF p.2 Section C, ten bands per family size one to four or more, 100% down to 10%, none above 20,815, 28,130, 35,445 and 42,760. Its first edges are the thresholds packet PDF p.3 prints (15,650, 21,150, 26,650, 32,150) and its last edges are 133 percent of them, rounded to the dollar ('incomes up to 133 percent of the threshold amount', PDF p.3). Packet PDF p.14: 'If your total MGI is $42,760 or less, you may qualify'; Form 740 PDF p.1 line 5 says the same of Columns A and B. Both printed examples (packet PDF p.26 and Schedule ITC PDF p.8: family of two at 22,650, 80%; family of four at 33,000, 90%) agree with the table. Schedule ITC PDF p.2 and Form 740 PDF p.2 line 21: the decimal multiplies Form 740 line 19, the tax after the personal tax credits, so credit_basis is tax with credit_rate 1. Family size is a household fact (qualifying children), not a filing status; the structured steps key family size one to 'single' and family size two to 'married_joint', and sizes three and four are in as_printed only.

Pension income exclusion: two layers that add. Schedule P line 4 = line 1(c) + the lesser of line 2 or 31,110. Line 1(c) has no dollar limit; the 31,110 limit applies only to income not in line 1(c). Each spouse computes their own.

Pensions from other states' governments: not named in the sources, and New York appears nowhere in them. Schedule P Part I takes only pension income 'paid by the federal government, by the Commonwealth of Kentucky, or by any Kentucky local government', and the Schedule P flowchart ends for anyone else with 'You do not need to file Schedule P. You are limited to $31,110 in excludable retirement.' Such a pension is 'pension and retirement income paid under a written retirement plan' (Schedule M PDF p.3), so public_pension_other_state is in ky_pension_exclusion and not in ky_pre1998_government_service. Judgement call: the kind is taken from those general words, not named. The reciprocity list on PDF p.22 covers wages and personal services, not pensions; no rule depends on the paying state, so paying_states is not used.

Disability retirement benefits, death benefits and deferred compensation reported on Form 1040 line 1 are eligible for the exclusion (Schedule M PDF p.3 and worksheet; Schedule P PDF p.2). Disability and death benefits have no income kind in the schema, so they are named in other_conditions only.

Schedule P PDF p.2 line 2 also takes amounts from Schedule M line 5 that reflect pension and IRA bases differences. Chart item 3 (PDF p.9): pensions and annuities starting after 7/1/86 and before 1/1/90 keep the 3-year recovery rule. Lump-sum distributions: special 10-year averaging on Form 4972-K (PDF p.13 Line 13). Not recorded as reliefs.
Not found in the booklet: any age, birth-year or income test on the pension exclusion.

Credit for tax paid to another state (Schedule ITC Section A line 6, PDF p.22-23), child and dependent care credit (20% of the federal credit, PDF p.14 Line 24), education tuition credit (Form 8863-K) and business incentive credits are not recorded as reliefs.
Other exempt items on the differences chart, not recorded as reliefs: Kentucky local government lease interest payments (item 9) and election workers' income (item 11).
Kentucky's Internal Revenue Code date is December 31, 2024 (PDF p.3). Qualified tips, overtime income and car loan interest are 'not deductible on the Kentucky return' (PDF p.3; PDF p.9 items 30-32).
Capital gains are not given a rate or a deducted share; the only different treatment printed is the two exempt items in capital_gains.
Surtaxes and recapture: none found in the booklet. Local occupational and license taxes are out of scope.

Indexing: the booklet says nothing about inflation adjustment of the rate, the standard deduction or the 31,110 limit. The family size thresholds are described as 'based on the federal poverty level' (PDF p.3); the booklet does not say how they change from year to year, so that entry stays not_stated with the wording in index.

Settlement 2026-11-07: capital_gains: A recorded none, B recorded eminent domain and Kentucky Turnpike Bond gains as exempt; PDF p.9 chart items 7 and 10 print both 'Exempt' and Schedule M PDF p.4 Line 14 lists eminent domain; kept B's two entries.
Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (killed in line of duty): A had no entry, B had one; PDF p.6 prints the exemption and Schedule M PDF p.4 Line 14 lists it; kept B's entry.

Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (Schedule P Part I): A split supplemental (Tier 2) railroad benefits into their own entry, B merged them with the pre-1998 government entry; Schedule P PDF p.1 line 1 and PDF p.2 apply the service-credit test only to the government pensions and take Tier 2 benefits whole; kept A's two entries.
Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (Tier 1 railroad): A had no entry, B had one; Schedule M PDF p.3 Line 10 prints 'Social Security equivalent U.S. Railroad Retirement Board benefits'; kept B's entry.
Settlement 2026-11-07: reliefs (Social Security) who.basis: A said each_person, B said return; Schedule M PDF p.3 Line 10 tests neither spouse and has no cap; return.

Settlement 2026-11-07: ky_pre1998_government_service covers military_pension: A and B agreed and both flagged it, and the point was sent back to be settled from the form. Schedule P's payer test is 'pension income paid by the federal government' (PDF p.2) and 'retired from the federal government' (PDF p.1). It names no military pension and excludes none; 'military' appears only for purchased service credit (PDF p.2 definitions and worksheet line 2). The packet's chart (PDF p.9 item 2) is the only printed statement on military retirement: its Kentucky cell, checked on the rendered page, sits against all three system lines including 'Federal and Military Retirement Systems' and says 'Partially exempt if retired after December 31, 1997; exempt if retired before January 1, 1998; Schedule P may be required'. The form's silence does not contradict the chart, so military_pension stays in covers.

measure.as_printed: Modified gross income is the greater of federal adjusted gross income adjusted to include interest income derived from municipal bonds (non-Kentucky) and lump-sum pension distributions not included in federal adjusted gross income; or Kentucky adjusted gross income adjusted to include lump-sum pension distributions not included in federal adjusted gross income. (Packet PDF p.11.) The worksheet (Schedule ITC PDF p.8; packet PDF p.26) also adds the spouse's federal AGI (line b) and the spouse's Kentucky AGI (line g) 'If married filing separate returns and living in the same household', and enters zero for an AGI of zero or less.

income_test.as_printed: Family Size Tax Credit Table (Schedule ITC Section C): credit is a percentage of Form 740 line 19 (tax after the personal tax credits), entered on line 21. Family size one: MGI not over 15,650 100%; over 15,650 to 16,276 90%; to 16,902 80%; to 17,528 70%; to 18,154 60%; to 18,780 50%; to 19,406 40%; to 19,876 30%; to 20,345 20%; to 20,815 10%; over 20,815 none. Family size two: 21,150 / 21,996 / 22,842 / 23,688 / 24,534 / 25,380 / 26,226 / 26,861 / 27,495 / 28,130. Family size three: 26,650 / 27,716 / 28,782 / 29,848 / 30,914 / 31,980 / 33,046 / 33,846 / 34,645 / 35,445. Family size four or more: 32,150 / 33,436 / 34,722 / 36,008 / 37,294 / 38,580 / 39,866 / 40,831 / 41,795 / 42,760. Each column ends at 133 percent of its threshold (packet PDF p.3). 'If your total MGI is $42,760 or less, you may qualify' (packet PDF p.14). Structured steps and threshold: 'single' holds the family size one column and 'married_joint' the family size two column, and threshold is each column's first edge, where the credit starts to fall; sizes three and four are in this text only.

indexing.index: CPI-U (US city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted): the prior year amount times the greater of 1 and the ratio of the average CPI-U for the 12 months ending the July 6 months before the tax year to the 12 months ending 18 months before; never falls; no rounding stated (the Department of Revenue publishes the amount) (statute PDF from the official Legislature page)

cite.publication: Kentucky Revised Statutes, section 141.081
cite.section: 141.081(2)(a): "For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2000, and each taxable year thereafter, the standard deduction for the current taxable year shall be equal to the standard deduction for the prior taxable year multiplied by the greater of: 1. The average of the monthly CPI-U figures for the twelve (12) consecutive months ending in and including the July six (6) months prior to the January beginning the current tax year, divided by the average of the monthly CPI-U figures for the twelve (12) months ending in and including the July eighteen (18) months prior to the January beginning the current tax year; or 2. One (1)."
